title_en: Provisions of the Supreme People's Court on Litigation Representatives' Access to Materials in Civil Cases

articles.content_en:
Article 1: Lawyers and other litigation agents representing parties in civil actions shall have the right to consult the relevant materials of the case they represent. However, the consultation of case materials by litigation agents shall not affect the adjudication of the case.
For the purpose of applying for a retrial, litigation agents may consult the relevant materials of the represented case that has been finally adjudicated.

Article 2: The People's Court shall provide convenient conditions for litigation agents to consult case files and arrange places for consultation. Where necessary, the clerk of the case or other staff members of the court shall be present.

Article 3: Where a litigation agent needs to consult the relevant materials of a case during the proceedings, he/she shall contact the clerk or the adjudication personnel of the case in advance; where consulting the relevant materials of a case whose adjudication has concluded, he/she shall contact the staff of the relevant department of the People's Court.

Article 4: A litigation agent consulting the relevant materials of a case shall present valid credentials such as a lawyer's license or identity card. When consulting the relevant materials of a case, he/she shall fill in the case file consultation form.

Article 5: The case materials consulted by a litigation agent during litigation shall be limited to the main files of the adjudication file and the enforcement file of the case, including the complaint, the written defense, court trial transcripts, and various evidentiary materials, etc.
After the adjudication of the case has concluded, the main file of the adjudication file may be consulted.

Article 6: After consulting the relevant materials of a case, the litigation agent shall promptly return all the case materials consulted to the clerk or other staff member responsible for keeping the case files.
The clerk or other staff members of the court shall check the case materials returned by the litigation agent on the spot, and after confirming that they are correct, shall sign on the case file consultation form. The case file consultation form shall be attached to the case file.
A litigation agent shall not take the consulted case materials out of the place designated by the court for case file consultation.

Article 7: A litigation agent may make excerpts from or copy the case materials consulted. Where case materials involve State secrets, they shall be handled in accordance with the relevant provisions of the State.
Copying case materials shall be subject to the consent of the case file custodian. Where copying the relevant materials of a case whose adjudication has concluded, the litigation agent may request the case file management department to affix a seal on the copies for confirmation.
Necessary fees may be charged for copying case materials.
Article 8: Where case materials consulted involve State secrets, trade secrets, or personal privacy, the litigation agent shall keep them confidential.

Article 9: When consulting case materials, a litigation agent shall not alter, damage, or remove any case materials.
The People's Court may handle a litigation agent who alters, damages, or removes case file materials by reference to the provisions of Item (1) of the first paragraph of Article 111 of the Civil Procedure Law.
Article 10: Where parties to a civil case consult the relevant case materials, these Provisions shall be applied by reference.

Article 11: These Provisions shall come into force as of the date of promulgation.
